what_it_does: When placing wires on a chip, engineers face a classic tension: shorter wires save space and power, but signals sometimes need longer detours to arrive at the right time (this timing requirement is called 'delay'). Existing routing tools let engineers dial in a preference — 'favor short wires' or 'favor tight timing' — but finding all the sensible trade-offs requires running the tool many times with different settings. PatLabor removes that trial-and-error by directly computing the full set of Pareto-optimal solutions — meaning every wire layout where you cannot improve timing without making the wire longer, and vice versa. For small wire groups (up to 9 connection points), it does this with provable accuracy and bounded running time, eliminating the need to guess at parameter values. The paper focuses on this theoretical guarantee; practical results for larger circuits would require reading the full text.
